rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is all-knowing and powerful, so whatever He does is deliberate and wise, and whatever He wills He can do.
rows.anchor: Çünkü O Alîm’dir, Kadîr’dir onun için her

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Direct revelation is a swift, hidden divine sign or an immediate casting of meaning into the heart; it ranges in intensity and may come awake or in sleep, to prophets and others.
rows.anchor: gayet serî‘ve hafî bir işaret hâlinde tefhim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech from behind a veil is created so that the hearer hears without seeing the speaker; Moses received speech in this way, and it reaches the hearing rather than being cast straight into the heart.
rows.anchor: bazı ecsâmda ve sâmi‘ada kelâm halk edip işittirir de, işiten kimin söylediğini görmez

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet’s report that revelation sometimes came like a bell’s ringing is assigned to speech heard from behind a veil.
rows.anchor: أَحْيَانًا يَأْتِينِي مِثْلَ صَلْصَلَةِ الْجَرَسِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third mode sends a messenger, usually an angel to prophets, who conveys what God wills; the angel’s form and whether the message is inward or audible can vary.
rows.anchor: bir resul, yani tebliğ vâsıtası bir melek gönderip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel’s revelation yields the strongest necessary knowledge; a messenger also witnesses between sender and recipient, strengthening the certainty of this mode.
rows.anchor: Cibrîl ile olan vahyin ifade ettiği ilm-i zarûrî hepsinden yüksek olur

rows.speaker: إمام أبو عبدالله تيمي اصفهاني
rows.claim: Taymī al-Isfahānī defines revelation by its root sense of conveying understanding: inspiration, gesture, and writing all qualify.
rows.anchor: İmam Ebû Abdullah Teymî İsfahânî

rows.speaker: راغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says revelation originally means a swift sign, conveyed through coded speech, bare sound, gesture, or writing.
rows.anchor: Râgıb da Müfredât’ında der ki

rows.speaker: راغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib applies revelation broadly to signs, satanic whispering, divine inspiration, direct hearing, a messenger, divine casting into the heart, inspiration, subjugation, and dreams.
rows.anchor: Ya müşahede olunan bir resul ile olur ki zâtı görülür kelâmı işitilir

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that revelation has ended while believers’ true dreams remain as glad tidings.
rows.anchor: vahiy kesildi mübeşşirât kaldı; mü’minin rüyası

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an uses the fourth-form verb for revelation; here the first mode is called wahy and messenger-mediated communication is called īḥāʾ, which can also mean causing revelation or sending.
rows.anchor: Lügaten vahyin fiili sülâsîden de gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No human receives God’s speech in any other mode or through ordinary face-to-face conversation, which a human could not bear.
rows.anchor: hiçbir beşere başka türlü söylemez. Beşerin beşerle konuşması gibi karşı karşıya ve apaçık mahdud bir suretle konuşmaz

rows.speaker: عبد الوهاب شعراني
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī says human nature blocks direct hearing of divine speech; when a servant cannot rise beyond it, God speaks through things and veiling manifestations.
rows.anchor: Hakk’ın kelâmını işitmekten men‘eden ancak beşeriyettir

rows.speaker: عبد الوهاب شعراني
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī says divine address requires the servant’s faculties to be strengthened; Moses fainted, the Prophet remained steadfast, and the mountain shattered.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ aleyhisselâm düştü bayıldı, zira o makama lâyık tecellîyi kabul edecek isti‘dâdı yoktu

rows.speaker: عبد الوهاب شعراني
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī holds that God’s inward speech to creation is everlasting: ʿUmar and inheriting saints recognize it, while others may mistake it for an ordinary occurrence.
rows.anchor: Şunu da bil Hak sübhânehû’nun halka hadîsi

rows.speaker: عبد الوهاب شعراني
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī distinguishes divine hadīth when a person answers God, mutual conversation when people answer each other, and address or speech when they listen to God.
rows.anchor: Eğer onunla Hak teâlâ’ya cevap veriyorlarsa ona ‘hadîs’ denir

rows.speaker: عبد الوهاب شعراني
rows.claim: For al-Shaʿrānī, revelation is divine address that gives its recipient knowledge; ordinary necessary knowledge in a person’s heart is not revelation unless it comes as address.
rows.anchor: bu sınıfını kendisine gelen kimsenin bir ilim istifade edebileceği bir kelâm yapmıştır

rows.speaker: عبد الوهاب شعراني
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī says saints receive inspiration through subtle traces extending from angelic spirits, not angels themselves; angels never descend with revelation or commands to nonprophets.
rows.anchor: evliyânın kalblerine ilham vahyinden inebilen ancak ervâh-ı melekiyeden uzanan bazı dakīkalardır, yoksa nefs-i melâike değildir

rows.speaker: عبد الوهاب شعراني
rows.claim: Prophetic revelation that legislates has ceased, but glad tidings remain; saints vary in mediated inspiration and cannot attain prophethood or establish an independent law.
rows.anchor: munkatı‘olan vahiy ancak teşrî‘vahyidir

rows.speaker: عبد الوهاب شعراني
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī says inspiration is only for good; its fullest form is guidance to follow revelation and remain within its limits.
rows.anchor: İlham ancak hayr hususunda olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech from behind a veil may be heard through a theophanic form that itself is the veil; the hearer understands the knowledge conveyed and knows the speaker is beyond it.
rows.anchor: o hitaptan delâlet ettiği ilim fehm olunur ve bilinir ki o bir hicabdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger may be an angel or a human envoy; only when such envoys transmit revealed divine words is their message God’s speech, not when they explain knowledge of their own.
rows.anchor: İkisi de Allah teâlâ’nın kelâmını tilâvet edenler gibi bilhassa nakleyledikleri zamandır

rows.speaker: عبد الوهاب شعراني
rows.claim: Some saints translate private inspiration from God: the written or spoken letters are the translator’s, while their spiritual meaning is God’s speech.
rows.anchor: söylenen veya yazılan harflerin suretleri mütercimin ve o suretlerin rûhu ise Allah’ın kelâmı olur

rows.speaker: عبد الوهاب شعراني
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī’s caution reflects the established theological principle that saints’ inspiration is not a general proof in creed and legal theory.
rows.anchor: enbiyâdan mâ‘adâsının ilhâmı umum için ilim sebeplerinden değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation is not merely an inward psychological event: it reports what lies beyond the self with certainty and has sensory, auditory, and inward aspects.
rows.anchor: vahiy, sırf enfüsî olan mücerred bir vicdan hâdisesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revealed Spirit means the Qur’an as a spiritual source of life, knowledge, and will; alternatively it means Gabriel, the trustworthy Spirit, sent with revelation.
rows.anchor: ilim, irade mebde’i gibi bir manevî hayat mebde’i olan Kur’ân’ı vahyettik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet could not have known scripture or the duties and conditions of faith by unaided judgment; obligation follows revealed law even if reason can know monotheism.
rows.anchor: tevhid bilinse de imanın vücûbu, yani teklif ve vazife

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without knowledge of scripture, worship remains imitation and conjecture rather than verified knowledge, as in the cited description of the unlettered.
rows.anchor: ilmî ve tahkīkī olmaz وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ إِلَّآ أَمَانِىَّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a light by which God guides whom He wills, and the Prophet guides people to the straight path, God’s own road rather than crooked routes under other authorities.
rows.anchor: onunla kullarımızdan dilediğimiz kimselere hidâyet edeceğiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the heavens and earth belong to God, all control and judgment are His; requests and obedience belong on His path, since all affairs ultimately return to Him.
rows.anchor: Bütün tasarruf hakkı O’nun, hüküm O’nun; onun için her ne istenecekse O’ndan istenilmek

none: Surah closing note, date, prayer, and next-surah heading only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation in truth entails justice: wrongs must be set right and good and evil cannot receive equal outcomes, so final recompense must occur in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: hak ile yaratış zâlimden mazlûmun hakkını alıvermek ve iyi ile kötüyü müsâvî tutmayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul is created to be recompensed without injustice: good receives good and evil receives evil, so the righteous and wicked cannot share the same future.
rows.anchor: her nefis hakları yenmeksizin kazandığıyla cezâlandırılmak, yani iyiye iyi, kötüye kötü karşılığı verilmek için yaratılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking desire as a god means refusing truth and making whatever pleases oneself an object of worship.
rows.anchor: gördün a şimdi o kimseyi ki ilâhını hevâsı ittihaz etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may let someone go astray despite knowledge; desire and lust blind the eye, deafen the ear, and numb the heart, even in philosophers and worldly-minded religious scholars.
rows.anchor: hevâ ve şehvet gözü kör, kulağı sağır, kalbi hissiz eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After God misguides someone, no one can guide him; the warning calls hearers to abandon desire and reason from knowledge toward the truth and final outcome.
rows.anchor: bırakarak ilmin muktezâsına göre bir düşünüp hakk u âkıbeti anlamayacak mısınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers claim earthly life is the only life: people die and live, and time alone destroys them; they deny any hereafter.
rows.anchor: dünya hayatımızdan başka hayat yoktur hayat denilen ondan ibarettir

rows.speaker: راغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines dahr as the span from the world’s beginning to its end, but also as a long duration or a person’s lifetime; as a verb noun it can mean a calamity overtaking someone.
rows.anchor: ‘Dehr’ âlemin vücûdunun başlangıcından nihâyetine kadar olan müddetin ismidir

rows.speaker: ابو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa suspends judgment on how long an indefinite, unqualified use of dahr denotes.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanife hazretleri nekre olan bu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Time is broader than dahr, covering short and long past, present, and future intervals; here al-dahr means time’s passing or length because the destruction is partial, not the end of the world.
rows.anchor: üç mânadan her birine haml olunabilir ise de en ziyade murûr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers have no knowledge for their claim about time’s power; they rely only on conjecture.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki buna dair bir ilimleri yoktur, onlar sade zannederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn say the scripture came after Moses because Jews and Christians alike recognize Moses, the Torah was the most exalted earlier scripture, and Jesus was also charged to follow it.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ aleyhisselâm iki ehl-i kitab beyninde müttefekun aleyhtir

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ offers another reason for naming Moses but not Jesus: the jinn were Jews.
rows.anchor: Atâ demiştir ki “çünkü Yehûd

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording indicates that jinn are not merely abstract beings; theologians describe them as subtle bodies.
rows.anchor: mütekellimîn bunlara “ecsâm-ı latîfe”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier scripture affirmed is either the Torah or all previous scriptures; guidance to truth means sound creed, while the straight way means revealed practical rulings that bring God’s approval.
rows.anchor: Önündekini, yani Tevrat’ı yahut bütün kütüb-i sâlifeyi tasdikliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification ‘some of your sins’ matters; one interpretation limits forgiveness to God’s rights, since conversion alone does not cancel debts or other established human claims.
rows.anchor: murad hâlis hakkullah olan günahlardır. Zira ibâdın hukūku mücerred iman ile mağfiret olunuvermez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although conversion erases a combatant’s prior bloodshed and plunder, it does not by itself cancel a prior personal debt or specified protected persons’ rights; the jinn promise only partial forgiveness to their people.
rows.anchor: mücerred İslâm’a gelmesiyle o borcun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever refuses God’s caller, meaning the Prophet and his envoys, cannot escape God’s punishment or find a protector apart from Him.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın davetçisine, yani Peygamber’e ve Peygamber’in elçilerine icâbet eylemezse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing creation means reasoning and inference: God created the heavens and earth without fatigue, refuting the claim that He rested after six days; Qāf 50:38 says no weariness touched Him.
rows.anchor: bu rü’yet göz görüşünden kalb görüşü ile re’y ve istidlâldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving the dead includes spiritual revival as well as bodily resurrection; God can restore life in every form, so believers gain eternal life while disbelievers enter Hell.
rows.anchor: ihyâya da şâmil olduğunda şüphe yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to be patient like the resolute messengers because he is one of them; azm means decisive commitment and steadfast pursuit of one’s purpose.
rows.anchor: ulü’l-azm resullerin sabrettiği gibi çünkü sen de onlardansın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean all messengers, since every prophet is resolute, or a subset distinguished by establishing law and enduring hardship; their famous names appear in Q 33:7.
rows.anchor: resuller olduğunu, resullerin hepsi azim sâhipleri bulunduğunu gösterir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also accepts that every prophet named in the Qur’an is among the resolute, since other messengers were not named in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Bizim fikrimizce Kur’an’da isimleri zikrolunan peygamberlerin hepsi ulü’l-azm rusüldür denilmek de doğrudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not hasten punishment for the disbelievers, especially the Quraysh; on seeing judgment, their worldly years will seem no longer than an hour because of the terror and length of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Sabret de onlar, o kâfirler, bâhusus Kureyş kâfirleri hakkında azâbı acele etme

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balāgh can mean either a sufficient, eloquent admonition or an eloquent conveyance, so no one can claim not to have heard the warning.
rows.anchor: Yeter yani bu size edilen va‘z u tezkir son derece beliğ, kâfi bir öğüttür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ultimately only rebellious people who leave obedience and refuse admonition are destroyed.
rows.anchor: Tâatten çıkmış öğüt dinlemez fâsık kavimdir

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī transmits from Anas that the Prophet advised reciting a supplication containing these verses when one asks for a need and wants it granted; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: Taberânî Duâ’da Enes’ten Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den

none: Continuation of the supplication quoted in the preceding segment; the report’s interpretive point is recorded there.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘backs of prostrations’ means remembrance after prayers, performed after every obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: secdelerin arkalarında, yani namazlardan sonra tesbih her namazın arkasında yapılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If tasbīḥ here means voluntary prayer, performing it after dawn or afternoon prayer is disliked.
rows.anchor: Nâfile namaz mânasına tesbih ise sabah ve ikindi namazlarından sonra mekruhtur

rows.speaker: كثيرون
rows.claim: Many commentators say the phrase points to the final sunnah prayer after Maghrib.
rows.anchor: son sünnetine işaret olduğunu söyleyenler de çoktur

rows.speaker: رازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī links the opening particle to what precedes: God equipped the Messenger with proof, wisdom, good exhortation, and argument, yet the disbelievers still refused faith.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ hidâyet ve dîn-i hak ile Resûlünü gönderdiğinde ona gereken her şeyi vermiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A debater’s apparent win need not prove his claim true; it may reflect intellectual strength and skill in assembling arguments.
rows.anchor: Bu beyan, müdde‘înin haklı olmasından değil, zihninin kuvvetinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators explain the negative particle in ‘fa-lā uqsimu’ as an extra rhythmic particle, an emphatic lām with an expanded vowel, or genuine negation; the author prefers genuine negation.
rows.anchor: bizce zâhir olan da budur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reinforces revealed signs and proofs with many oaths, especially in early and final-period surahs, because people who cannot debate may claim truth while blaming their opponent for unfairness.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ inzal buyurduğu âyât ve delâilini bir de türlü kasemlerle teyid buyurmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred reading the oath means ‘No, the matter is not as they think; I swear’, or that no further argument is needed before swearing.
rows.anchor: iş öyle zannettikleri gibi değil, yemin ederim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possible literal referents of the stars’ stations include their setting or rising places, celestial positions and mansions, meteor-fall locations, or where stars fall at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: yıldızlar demek olduğuna göre mevkileri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more fitting sense is the successive portions of the Qur’an revealed at each descent; this allusion is intended at least by double entendre, so ‘stars’ should not be translated literally.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın necimleri yani her tenzilde indirilen kısımları mânasına olmak daha muvâfıktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Qur’anic sense, the stations may encompass angels, the Prophet, memorizer-hearts, written pages, meanings, and the occasions or rulings prompting revelation.
rows.anchor: ıtlak olunanların hepsine şumûlü en muvâfık mâna olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause ‘if you knew’ interrupts the oath’s assertion, while the next declaration that it is a noble Qur’an is the oath’s answer.
rows.anchor: Mu‘teriza içinde mu‘terizadır. {إِنَّهُۥ لَقُرْءَانٌۭ} Kasemin cevabıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karīm can mean richly beneficial because the Qur’an contains key knowledge for life and the afterlife, beautiful and worthy of honor, or honored with God.
rows.anchor: çok faydalı, feyizli, çünkü me‘âş ve me‘âda müte‘allik birçok mühim ilimlerin esaslarını muhtevîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden book is safeguarded against impurity and loss; only the purified may touch it, understood as a prohibition against contact by ritually or spiritually impure hands.
rows.anchor: saklı, yani temiz tutulmak, kirletilmemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse grounds the juristic rules that a ritually impure person may not recite the Qur’an and someone without ablution may not touch the mushaf.
rows.anchor: cünüb iken Kur’an okunamayacağı ve abdesti olmayanın mushafa messedemeyeceği beyan olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a revelation sent down from the Lord of all worlds.
rows.anchor: Rabbü’l-âlemîn tarafından indirilmiş bir tenzildir o

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke asks whether people will dishonor or defile the Qur’an and make disbelief their only share of its blessing, showing ingratitude instead of benefiting from it.
rows.anchor: bu kelâma mı yağ süreceksiniz hürmetsizlik edip inkâr veya tahâretsizlikle onu kirletmeye mi kalkışacaksınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul reaching the throat is the final agony before death; relatives watch the dying person’s distress but are powerless to rescue them.
rows.anchor: son ihtizar vakti demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is nearer to the dying person in knowledge, power, and control; observers see only outward signs and cannot perceive the inward state or remove it.
rows.anchor: Gerek ilim gerek kudret gerek tasarruf cihetiyle her hususta yakınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks deniers who reject judgment to return the departing soul if they are truthful; the clause also supplies the response to the preceding conditional, exposing their helplessness under God’s rule.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın dinine tâbi‘olmamak, vahdâniyetle rubûbiyetini tanımamak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muqarrabīn are the foremost of the three classes named at the surah’s opening; rawḥ means rest, mercy, gladness, or enduring life, rayḥān good provision, and the Garden of Bliss joy without grief.
rows.anchor: rahat, rahmet, ferah, hayât-ı dâime mânalarına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the right are identified by the same title as before, and their greeting to one another is reported to them from God.
rows.anchor: birbirlerine selâmını taraf-ı ilâhîden ihbardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lying, misguided are the people of the left; ‘misguided’ is an explanatory epithet, echoing their description in Q 56:51.
rows.anchor: ki bunlar ashâb-ı şimâldir ki

rows.speaker: ابن عطية، رازي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s explanation, preferred by al-Rāzī, reads ‘truth of certainty’ as intensification like ‘truth of truth’: certainty’s highest level, beyond which there is no attainment.
rows.anchor: En muvâfıkı İbn Atıyye’nin beyânı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Certainty has three degrees: knowledge, direct vision, and lived realization; ḥaqq al-yaqīn is truth embodied in actual experience beyond knowledge and observation.
rows.anchor: bilfiil içinde tahakkuk ile yaşanan hakikattir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further account describes ḥaqq al-yaqīn as the servant’s annihilation in God and abiding through Him in knowledge, vision, and state; knowing death, seeing angels, and tasting death illustrate the three levels.
rows.anchor: abdin Hak’ta fânî olması ve O’nunla yalnız ilmen değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final glorification is the surah’s refrain: even if disbelievers refuse, the Messenger should praise and sanctify God by His mighty name.
rows.anchor: Bu sûrenin de tercî‘âyeti budur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close links backward to the surah’s account and forward to the next surah: the Messenger should join the whole cosmos in glorifying God, whose name is supreme.
rows.anchor: Bütün göklerde ve yerdeki mevcûdât Allah’ı tesbih eder

none: The segment contains only the translated verse text; no commentary beyond it.
